identity.title: Brain Treebank: Large-scale intracranial recordings from naturalistic language stimuli

problem.claim: Build a large-scale intracranial neural dataset aligned with naturalistic, linguistically annotated movie stimuli, and analyze language-sensitive electrodes over time.

contributions.claim: Introduces the Brain Treebank: intracranial electrophysiological recordings from 10 subjects watching Hollywood movies, aligned with corrected transcripts, word onsets, and UD parses.
Analyzes electrode sensitivity to language features and provides a rough temporal mapping of language processing across electrodes.
Makes the Brain Treebank available online.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe it as the largest intracranial dataset featuring grounded naturalistic language, among the largest English UD treebanks, and one of few UD treebanks aligned to multimodal features.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Authors report 43 total hours of recordings, with subjects viewing an average of 2.6 movies for 4.3 hours.
Authors report over 38,000 sentences and 223,000 words, with subjects averaging 168 implanted electrodes.
Authors report an electrode-sensitivity analysis and a rough language-processing time course across electrodes.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper presents intracranial recordings collected while 10 subjects watched one or more Hollywood movies.
Movie audio was transcribed and corrected, word onsets were manually annotated, and transcripts were converted into manually corrected UD parses.

The resource spans tens of thousands of sentences and hundreds of thousands of words, and is positioned as unusually large for grounded intracranial language data and multimodally aligned UD resources.
The authors analyze language-sensitive electrodes and their rough processing time course, then provide the dataset online.

source_observation.claim: The resource aligns neural recordings with multiple linguistic and temporal annotations, including word onsets, parts of speech, and dependency parses.

lessons.interpretation: Layered alignment can connect a shared naturalistic stimulus to distinct explanatory levels without reducing the resource to a single label.
lessons.application: For another multimodal dataset, define annotation layers that support both event timing and structured interpretation, and state how each layer enables a distinct analysis.
lessons.exception: This approach may be unsuitable when annotation cost is prohibitive or when the target question requires only a narrowly defined signal label.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify recording locations, electrode coverage variability, subject demographics, movie identities, or preprocessing details.
The reported analysis is not quantified; no sensitivity metrics, temporal estimates, baselines, or statistical conditions are given.
The abstract does not provide evidence for the stated size comparisons beyond the authors' characterization.
